title: Base rates: single-event and few-event anomalies in direct detection (2008-2026) and other rare-event searches, and what they did next
question: How often have ~2.5-4 sigma local single-event, few-event or small-excess anomalies in direct detection and other rare-event searches turned out to be signal, background/artefact or unresolved; how fast and by what route were they resolved; what prior P(DM) does the base rate imply for the LZ event and what posterior with P027's B_DM; and when and how should the LZ event be resolved?
headline_result: In a recalled reference class of 45 anomalies (43 primary), 0 of 25 resolved new-physics ~3 sigma hints were real versus 4 of 5 hints of a predicted process; the direct-detection new-physics base rate is r = 0.062 (Jeffreys, 0/7 resolved; 95% one-sided < 0.23), which coincides with P061's log-uniform prior median (pi_DM 0.017 <-> r 0.055) and via P061 Eq. 3 gives P(DM | LZ event) = 0.012 (68% 0.001-0.052) centrally, 0.059 (0.005-0.22) optimistically; new-physics anomalies with a comparable independent test resolve in a median 3 yr (25/46/54/71% by 1/2/3/5 yr), 52% via an independent experiment
key_numbers: 45 items (28 certain, 15 likely, 2 uncertain excluded), 11 DD, 10 few-event, 24 in 2.5-4 sigma, 13 unresolved; outcomes 9 statistical, 7 contradicted, 4 artefact, 3 background, 3 theory revision, 4 real; P(real): DD new 0/7 -> 0.062 (0.003-0.13, <0.23), all new 0/25 -> 0.019 (<0.073), in-window new 0/13 -> 0.036, expected process 4/5 -> 0.75; unresolved-as-real envelope 0.17/0.29; recall correction 0.022-0.062; KM comparable-test stratum F(1,2,3,5 yr) = 0.25/0.46/0.54/0.71, median 3 yr; no-test stratum F(5) = 0.27; routes independent 52%, more data 16%, reanalysis 12%, theory 12%, hardware 8%; P(DM|LZ) 0.012 central, 0.059 optimistic, 0.0036 pessimistic, naive 0.34-0.48; implied pi_DM 0.009 (<0.08); P(r >= 0.25) = 4%; LZ resolution 46% by 2028, median 2029
model_or_mechanism: Outside-view reference class compiled from memory with reliability flags; Beta-binomial (Jeffreys) base rates by stratum with unresolved-as-null/real brackets; odds-ratio recall-bias and dilution corrections; Kaplan-Meier survival with right-censoring at Sept 2026; P061 Eq. 3 reference-class posterior with r drawn from the Beta posterior; log-log translation of r to P061's implied pi_DM
stance: statistical reassessment (weakens: historical base rate for unpredicted ~3 sigma anomalies is <~ 0.06, consistent with P061's central prior)
confidence: low - compilation is recalled and incomplete, outcome coding is judgement, zero-count posteriors are prior-driven
